thread.title: Dividend Aristocrats NOBL Vs. Achievers VIG, Head To Head - The First 5 Years - ProShares S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats ETF (BATS:NOBL)

author: Dale Roberts
title: Dividend Aristocrats NOBL Vs. Achievers VIG, Head To Head - The First 5 Years - ProShares S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats ETF (BATS:NOBL)
text:
The Dividend Appreciation Index fund Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF ( VIG ) was launched in May of 2006. The fund tracks the US Nasdaq Dividend Achievers Select Index. Constituents have increased their dividends, each year for 10 years or more. The index applies a proprietary dividend health screen. The Index Fund was launched in May of 2006 and has a history of slight outperformance vs. the iShares Core S&P 500 ETF ( IVV ) from inception with lesser volatility. Once again companies that offer a meaningful dividend growth history have that potential to deliver those superior risk-adjusted returns.
Portfolio 1 is VIG. The chart is courtesy of portfoliovisualizer.com As always, past performance does not guarantee future returns.
We see a slight, but meaningful enough outperformance from 2006, and we see lesser volatility and a lesser drawdown in the financial crisis. The Dividend Appreciation Fund simply offered better risk-adjusted returns for the period. That is the attraction for many who embrace dividend growth investing; you can include my name on that list.
I have been studying the Dividend Achievers and the top holdings for many years. You can start with this article from 2012, The Scaredy Cat Vanguard Dividend Appreciation Portfolio . In that article, I track and list the Top 10 holdings from inception and through to 2012. You'll find other Top 10, 15 and Top 20 articles from the Dale Roberts articles list.
And this article might be described as almost 'shocking' - Original Dividend Achievers Top 10, This Should Not Have Worked .
In that article we see the top holdings and the performance through the Financial Crisis. Those holdings outperform through the correction and for several years. It contains 2 of 10 companies being 'financials' heading into a financial crisis. It should not have worked, but it did.
Here's the original top 10 holdings of Vanguard's Dividend Appreciation Fund (NYSEARCA: VIG ) - those companies are Chevron (NYSE: CVX ), Exxon Mobil (NYSE: XOM ), Procter & Gamble (NYSE: PG ), Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO ), IBM (NYSE: IBM ), GE (NYSE: GE ), Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ ), Walmart (NYSE: WMT ), PepsiCo (NYSE: PEP ), and AIG (NYSE: AIG ).
Given the potential better risk-adjusted returns of Achievers, I purchased 15 of the largest Dividend Achievers in early 2015. Please have a read of Buying Dividend Growth Stocks Without Looking .
I didn't look, but we know the index sure looks. I have continued to buy and hold and add, still without looking.
Is a greater dividend growth history more advantageous? The Dividend Aristocrat Index insists on 25 years of dividend growth. And many on Seeking Alpha know of the history of better risk-adjusted returns of the Aristocrats vs. The Market.
ProShares made the index investable by way of ProShares S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats ETF ( NOBL ) back in 2013.
The Achievers and Aristocrat constituents have been battle-tested through recessions and severe market corrections. A massive distinction of course is that the Aristocrats have had to increase their dividends through two market corrections. If we seek greater financial health and dividend sustainability, logic might suggest that it might be advantage Aristocrats.
The dividend growth indexes have a very conservative stance. Here's the sector breakdown for the Achievers.
We see that the index has virtually eliminated any energy representation, the sector does not even register.
And here's the Aristocrat allocation.
The two indices have near equal representation in the most conservative baskets of consumer and healthcare sectors. The Achievers have that tech basket that we might see as more growth-oriented.
If we look at the current top 10 holdings of VIG we see a very solid Aristocrat core bookended by two growth stories in Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Nike ( NKE ). Texas Instruments ( TXN ) is the other larger cap tech holding. We hold those three growth companies, again skimmed in 2015.
Here are the current top 10 holdings of NOBL. Here's the daily holdings page from ProShares.
Checking in on the performance of the ETF NOBL we see, as expected.
The fund delivered outperformance during periods of market volatility.
And to year-end 2018 from portfoliovisualizer. Portfolio 1 is NOBL.
Once again, the minor market correction was the great equalizer. The Aristocrats moved back into the lead. Again, the Aristocrats and that meaningful dividend growth history are delivering better risk-adjusted returns, even though we've only experienced modest corrections and volatility.
Too many investment writers (and indexers) fail to recognize the dividend growth advantage or benefits. I am an outlier in that I include dividend options on my Model ETF page . And I'll write on dividend managed portfolio options.
So what about the Achievers vs. Aristocrats? Portfolio 1 is NOBL. Portfolio 2 is VIG. Once again it's advantage NOBL - it's advantage greater dividend growth history. The Achievers Index ran into more trouble in 2015 due to energy names and the healthcare basket. It's fighting back and is catching up in this short-term race.
Here's the annual returns breakdown.
Recently we see the Achievers hold up modestly better in 2018. Maybe that's a good sign for the index? From 2016, VIG has been outperforming NOBL by almost 1% annual.
I think VIG will beat NOBL in total returns over the longer term.
Of course, that's why I skimmed 'em. But again, our 15 Achievers do include 9 Aristocrats. Our 15 companies follow that top 15 Achievers framing of a solid Aristocrat core and some growth orientation around the fringes.
Here's our equal-weight 15 Dividend Achievers 15 as Portfolio 1 from January of 2015 to end of 2018. We see some slight outperformance for the index skimming. And even slightly better risk-adjusted returns.
I'll admit I am surprised at that. This is the first time I've benchmarked the index skimming exercise against the Aristocrats. Some of the outperformance of course is due to the fee structure on the ETF at .35%.
Obviously, my take is that we can simply buy enough of 'em to replicate the index. You can even potentially shade your performance with selection criteria - greater growth vs. greater stability.
For our US portfolio we also have 3 picks by way of Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), BlackRock ( BLK ) and Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.B ) (NYSE: BRK.A ). That improves on the outperformance vs. the Aristocrats. Portfolio 1 is our 18 US holdings.
Chalk one up for simplicity and investing without second guessing.
Who will win the long-term race? VIG or NOBL Where would you put your money? What index fund would you buy? What index fund would you skim?
In advance I appreciate your thoughts and comments.
